property_summary: For any correct clone, `c.owner()` must return the address of the owner (offset 0) and never the collateral address (offset 0x14); the mutant returns the collateral, so these two values differ.

For any correctly cloned Cooler with an owner different from its collateral token, c.owner() must return the deployer address, not the collateral token address; the mutant returns the collateral token address instead.

For any clone C, owner() must return the address embedded at immutable args offset 0x0 (the deployer), which differs from the collateral address returned by collateral(), whereas the mutant returns collateral(), so owner() != collateral() always holds in the reference but fails when owner() == collateral() in the mutant.

Every clone's owner() must return the address at immutable args offset 0x0 (the deployer), not the address at offset 0x14 (the collateral token), so the value returned by owner() must always differ from the value returned by collateral().

For any clone C, calling owner() must return the deployer address (offset 0x0), not the collateral token address (offset 0x14); the mutant swaps them, so when owner and collateral differ, owner() differs from collateral() in the reference but equals collateral() in the mutant.

The owner() function must always return the same address that was deployed via clone with owner at offset 0x0; the buggy version returns the debt token address at offset 0x28 instead, so they differ and owner() returns a different address than the original deployer/owner.

For any Cooler instance created by CoolerFactory.generateCooler, the address returned by C.owner() must equal the address returned by _getArgAddress(0x0) (the original deployer/owner packed into immutable args), but the mutant uses _getArgAddress(0x28) which returns the debt token address, so the equality owner() == factory caller fails for some non-degenerate input.

For any Cooler created by the factory, the owner() must match the immutable arg at offset 0x0 (the original deployer), but the mutant uses offset 0x28 (debt token), so owner() equals debt() when the same address is used for owner and debt, violating the invariant that owner() should never equal debt() for well-formed distinct inputs.

For any valid Cooler clone instance, calling owner() must return the address that was passed as the first immutable arg (msg.sender to the factory) at offset 0x0, but the buggy version returns the address at offset 0x28 (debt token), which differs whenever the debt token address is not equal to the factory caller.

For any Cooler clone created by the factory, the `owner()` address must equal the immutable argument at offset 0x0 (the original factory caller), but the buggy version reads offset 0x28 (debt token), so they differ whenever the debt token is not the original deployer.

The owner() function must always return the address of the contract's owner, which is derived from a specific immutable argument offset, not the factory address. The mutant incorrectly returns the factory address, causing owner() to return a different value for any contract instance.

For any Cooler deployment, the owner() view must return the 0x0 immutable arg (owner) and factory() must return the 0x3c arg (factory); the mutant makes owner() also return the factory arg, so owner() equals factory() in the mutant for every deployment, while it never equals in the reference.

For any Cooler contract clone, calling owner() and factory() must return different addresses, but the mutant makes them return the same address because owner() incorrectly reads the factory's immutable arg slot.

For any Cooler contract clone, owner() and factory() must return different addresses; the mutant makes owner() also return factory() so they become equal, breaking the invariant that the owner and factory are distinct entities.
For any clone of C, the owner() and factory() addresses are always different, but the mutant makes owner() return the factory address, so owner() equals factory() for every clone.
The collateral() function must return the address encoded in the clone's immutable args, not a hardcoded address; the bug returns 0x01 instead.

For any clone deployed via the factory, the collateral() function must return the same address stored in its immutable arguments, but the bug returns a hardcoded 0x01, so any factory-deployed clone will violate the invariant that collateral() equals the address passed in the immutable args data.

For any deployment where the owner and collateral addresses are distinct, the collateral() function must return the collateral address (offset 0x14), not the owner address (offset 0x0). The bug returns owner at offset 0x0 instead of collateral, breaking this invariant.

For any deployed C clone with immutable args where the collateral address (offset 0x14) and the owner address (offset 0x0) are distinct, the collateral() function must return the per-deployment collateral address; the mutant returns the owner address instead.

The collateral() view function must return the collateral token address (offset 0x14) from immutable args, not the debt token address; the buggy version returns the debt token address (offset 0x28), violating this rule for any contract deployment.

The collateral() function must return the address at immutable args offset 0x14 (collateral token), not offset 0x28 (debt token); the buggy version returns the debt token, so for any clone deployed with different collateral and debt tokens, the returned address equals the debt token instead of the collateral token.

For any clone deployed via the factory, calling collateral() must return the address that was passed as the collateral token (the one used in generateCooler), not the debt token; the buggy version always returns the debt token address regardless of the tokens used, so when the two tokens are different the returned address equals the debt token instead of the collateral token.

For any clone deployed through CoolerFactory, the address returned by collateral() must equal the address of the collateral token used in generateCooler (which can be retrieved via the factory's coolersFor mapping), not the debt token; the buggy version returns the debt token address, so when collateral and debt differ, asserting equality between collateral() and the collateral token known to the factory fails.

The collateral() view function must return the collateral token address (offset 0x14) from immutable args, not the debt token address; the buggy version returns the debt token address (offset 0x28), violating this rule for any clone deployment with distinct collateral and debt tokens.
The `debt()` function must return the address of the debt token set at creation time, not address(0). The bug violates this by always returning address(0).
For any factory-generated cooler, the debt() function must return the debt token address that was originally encoded during clone creation, not address(0).

For any Cooler contract (C) created via the factory, calling debt() must return the debt token address that was encoded during clone creation, and not address(0). The mutant violates this by always returning address(0), so its return value will differ from the reference for any non-zero debt token address.
